    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's voice reaches the surrendered heart in samādhi — Brahmā hears, then transmits without delay; our work is to listen inwardly and obey at once.
    Practical Applications
    • Sit in silence before your morning duties and listen for Kṛṣṇa's guidance through the heart (caitya-guru) rather than scrolling for outside opinions.
    • Notice the next clear instruction you receive from guru, śāstra, or conscience today, and execute it āśu — immediately, without the usual delay of debate.
    • Refuse the mūḍha view that Kṛṣṇa is an ordinary historical figure; speak of Him today as the living Supreme Person who still instructs His devotees from within.
    Reflection Questions
    • When the Lord's instructions arrive through the heart in trance, am I sitting still enough — through japa, śravaṇa, and svādhyāya — to actually hear, or is my inner space so crowded with my own commentary that even Brahmā's reception couldn't penetrate?
    • Which order from guru, śāstra, or sādhus have I already 'heard' but quietly delayed — and what does Brahmā's āśu tathaiva mā ciram (do it now, without delay) expose about my preferred mode of obedience?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Before opening any feed today, sit for five minutes in deliberate silence — your version of samādhi as a beginner — and notice what 'voice' actually has access to your heart when the noise stops.
    • Pick one instruction you have already received from a trustworthy elder (parent, teacher, devotee mentor) and execute it tathaiva mā ciram — exactly as told, without delay — instead of negotiating it down to something easier.
    • Watch how your friend group handles a directive from a coach, professor, or senior — who delays, who edits the message, who acts cleanly? Locate yourself honestly in that pattern and adjust this week.
    householder
    • Treat your morning sādhana as the channel — if you skip it, do not be surprised when family decisions later in the day feel reactive rather than guided; protect that time the way Brahmā protects his samādhi.
    • When you receive a clear instruction from śāstra or guru about money, children, or work, do not let it sit in 'I'll think about it' — translate it into one concrete action this week, the way the demigods translated Viṣṇu's order into immediate execution.
    • In your role as the 'Brahmā' of your household — the one who passes guidance to children and dependents — examine whether you are softening Kṛṣṇa's message to make it palatable, or transmitting it cleanly with the diacritics intact.
    senior
    • Use the diminishing demands of this stage to deepen the listening — what younger life would not give you the silence for, age is now offering; do not waste it on television and grievance.
    • Identify one mentee — a grandchild, a younger devotee, a colleague — and accept the Brahmā-role consciously: you are the link in the chain now, and what you transmit (or fail to transmit) will outlive you.
    • When the body sends its own 'instructions' — pain, fatigue, the nearness of death — practice hearing through them rather than being deafened by them, so that Kṛṣṇa's voice in the heart remains the loudest signal in the room.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating 'hearing in the heart' as license for personal intuition or feelings — confusing the mind's whispers with Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu's actual instruction, which arrives only through the bona fide paramparā and the Bhāgavatam, not through one's own ahaṅkāra.
    • Drifting into impersonalism by equating Brahmā's inward reception with a generic 'inner voice' or 'higher Self,' when the verse insists on a specific personal Lord (Viṣṇu) speaking and a specific person (Brahmā) hearing and faithfully relaying.
    • Hearing the message but stalling on transmission and execution — savoring the contemplative 'samādhi' phase while neglecting the punar vidhīyatām āśu duty to immediately carry the order to those one is responsible for (family, students, juniors).
    Discussion Prompts
    • Brahmā hears Viṣṇu only because he is in samādhi — not because Viṣṇu spoke louder. Where in your own life are you waiting for Kṛṣṇa to 'speak louder' instead of doing the work to quiet the receiver? Push back honestly on each other if someone offers a tidy answer.
    • Prabhupāda compares hearing Viṣṇu in trance to a telephone — modern science only catches up to what yogīs already did. Is this comparison persuasive to you, or does it feel apologetic? Defend your actual position to your partner, not the 'devotee' position.
    • The verse turns on a chain of command: Viṣṇu instructs Brahmā, Brahmā instructs the demigods, the demigods act 'without delay.' Where in your life are you the demigod who delays? Where are you the Brahmā who hears but softens the message before passing it on?
    Role Play

    Two students. Student A is a senior devotee who has just come out of japa and feels strongly that the group should change a service arrangement — they say it 'came in meditation.' Student B is a thoughtful but skeptical peer who wants evidence, not impressions. Role-play a 5-minute conversation where A must convey what they heard with the gravity of Brahmā addressing the demigods (śṛṇuta — hear me, and act without delay), while B presses on the difference between Brahmā's qualified hearing and ordinary mental impressions. The teacher then asks: how would each of you actually verify the instruction before acting tathaiva mā ciram?

    Objections & Responses
    • Hearing Viṣṇu 'in the sky' while in trance sounds like auditory hallucination dressed up in Sanskrit. Why should a modern person take this literally?
      We are not asked to take Brahmā's hearing as a private psychological event — it is a transmission within a lineage that produced the Vedas, the Bhāgavatam, and a continuous tradition of realized teachers whose instructions, when followed, yield observable change in the practitioner. Prabhupāda himself uses the telephone analogy not to flatter science but to point out that subtle transmission of sound at a distance is not, in principle, absurd to the modern mind. The real question is not whether the channel exists but whether you have purified the receiver — hṛdā, the heart — enough to trust what you hear. Until then, you do not rely on private audition; you rely on guru, sādhu, and śāstra. That is the safeguard against hallucination.
    • If Viṣṇu can speak only to Brahmā and Brahmā alone passes it down, this is just spiritual hierarchy protecting itself. Why can't Kṛṣṇa speak directly to me?
      He does — through the caitya-guru in the heart, through the dīkṣā- and śikṣā-guru, through śāstra, and ultimately through the holy name, which is non-different from Him. The verse is not gate-keeping; it is describing how revelation is structured so that it remains undistorted. Brahmā receives, the demigods execute — and notice that even Brahmā does not freelance; he says 'hear from me the order of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu,' attributing it carefully. The hierarchy is not a wall between you and Kṛṣṇa; it is the very means by which His words reach you uncorrupted. Bypass it and you will hear plenty of voices, but they will mostly be your own ahaṅkāra speaking in a Sanskrit accent.
    Analogy

    Brahmā in trance hears Viṣṇu's words in the sky — like a junior officer in headquarters receiving radio orders from supreme command. He does not improvise the response; he repeats the order to the assembled troops. The verse's mechanism is paramparā at the cosmic level: receive accurately, transmit promptly.

    Important Words
    • puṁsā — by the Supreme Personality of Godhead
      Instrumental of puṁs, 'the Person.' Throughout this passage the Lord is named as Person, not principle. Bhagavān's foreknowledge is a personal act — He knows because He sees, not because of a structural omniscience.
    • avadhṛtaḥ — was certainly known
      Past participle of ava-dhṛ, 'to ascertain, determine.' The verse establishes timing — the knowing preceded the asking. Prayer in Gauḍīya is therefore never information-delivery; it is the devotee's participation in what is already underway.
    • aṁśaiḥ — expanding as plenary portions
      Instrumental plural of aṁśa. The demigods will descend not in their full personal form but as aṁśas. The verse models a principle: even servants of Bhagavān take partial expansions when entering the līlā. Multiplicity of presence is normal in Vaikuṇṭha-tattva.
    • īśvara-īśvaraḥ — the Lord of lords
      The lords' lord — Bhagavān as supreme even over the īśvaras (controllers) like Brahmā, Śiva, Indra. The compound rules out any hierarchy in which the Person could be balanced against other 'gods' — the demigods themselves are subordinate.
    • sva-kāla-śaktyā — by His own potency the time factor
      Sva (own) + kāla (time) + śakti (potency). Time is not external to Bhagavān; it is His śakti. Therefore He 'moves on earth diminishing burden by His own time-energy' — the same kāla that frightens the conditioned soul is His instrument in His hand.
    Lord Brahmā informed the demigods: Before we submitted our petition to the Lord, He was already aware of the distress on earth. Consequently, for as long as the Lord moves on earth to diminish its burden by His own potency in the form of time, all of you demigods should appear through plenary portions as sons and grandsons in the family of the Yadus.
    Purport

    As stated in the Brahma-saṁhitā (5.39) : rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan nānāvatāram akarod bhuvaneṣu kintu kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṁ samabhavat paramaḥ pumān yo govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi “I worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Govinda, who is always situated in various incarnations such as Rāma, Nṛsiṁha and many sub-incarnations as well, but who is the original Personality of Godhead, known as Kṛṣṇa, and who incarnates personally also.” In this verse from Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam we find the words puraiva puṁsāvadhṛto dharā-jvaraḥ. The word puṁsā refers to Kṛṣṇa, who was already aware of how the whole world was suffering because of the increase of demons. Without reference to the supreme power of the Personality of Godhead, demons assert themselves to be independent kings and presidents, and thus they create a disturbance by increasing their military power. When such disturbances are very prominent, Kṛṣṇa appears. At present also, various demoniac states all over the world are increasing their military power in many ways, and the whole situation has become distressful. Therefore Kṛṣṇa has appeared by His name, in the Hare Kṛṣṇa movement, which will certainly diminish the burden of the world. Philosophers, religionists, and people in general must take to this movement very seriously, for man-made plans and devices will not help bring peace on earth. The transcendental sound Hare Kṛṣṇa is not different from the person Kṛṣṇa. nāma cintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇaś caitanya-rasa-vigrahaḥ pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto ’bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ ( Padma Purāṇa ) There is no difference between the sound Hare Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa the person.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Lord Brahmā informed the demigods: Before we submitted our petition to the Lord, He was already aware of the distress on earth. Consequently, for as long as the Lord moves on earth to diminish its burden by His own potency in the form of time, all of you demigods should appear through plenary portions as sons and grandsons in the family of the Yadus.
    Commentary

    Braham repeats the words of Visnu in four verses. Pumsa here means bhagavan Krsna, because Srimad Bhagavatam describes Krsna as the person who would appear to relieve the problems of the earth: krsnah svayam samabhavat paramah puman ya (Krsna himself who is the supreme being (puman) appeared.) The sufferings of the earth have been understtond (avadhrtah) already by Krsna (pumsa). The devas should appear along with to the Lord’s associates such as Uddhava and Satyaki who are expansions of the Lord (amsaih) in the family of Yadu (Kurus, or more specifically the Pandavas). Isvaresvara indicates that Krsna is the Lord of all of lords (isvaras) including Visnu.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Brahmā repeated Viṣṇu’s words in four verses. Kṛṣṇa (puṁsā), of whom I (Viṣṇu) am a portion of a portion, has already understood the distressful condition of the earth. You do not have to inform him. I (Viṣṇu) also know. Therefore I did not become visible personally to hear about it at this time. You should be born along with the unlimited portions of Kṛṣṇa. The portions are the Yādavas: ete hi yādavāḥ sarve mad gaṇā eva bhāmini sarvadā mat priyā devi mat tūlya-guṇa-śālinaḥ O goddess! All the Yādavas are my people, most dear to me and equal to me in qualities. Padma Purāṇa, Kartika-māhātmya You should be born as sons and grandsons of the Yādavas, who are eternal associates of the Lord and remain near them. Yadāvas also includes their relatives the Pāṇḍavas. It should be understood that the Pāṇḍavas attained Svarga (in Mahābhārata), but being qualified as eternal associates, actually went to the Lord. Kṛṣṇa is the lord of all of us, the lord of the universal form and antaryāmī. īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ anādir ādir govindaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam || Kṛṣṇa is the supreme controller. He is the enjoyer of innumerable consorts, and the possessor of an eternal form of knowledge and bliss. Though, he is without origin, he is the source of all other forms of God, and is the cause of all causes. He is Govinda, the boy who cares for the cows. Brahma-saṁhitā 1 yasyaika-niśvasita-kālam athāvalambya jīvanti loma-vilajā jagad-aṇḍa-nāthāḥ | viṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo govindam ādi-puruṣaṁ tam ahaṁ bhajāmi || I worship the Supreme Lord Govinda whose first expansion is Mahā-viṣṇu, who determines the appearance and disappearance of the rulers within the universe (even Kṣirodakaśāyī-viṣṇu) by his exhalation and inhalation of breath. Brahma-saṁhitā 48 athāham aṁśa-bhāgena devakyāḥ putratāṁ śubhe prāpsyāmi tvaṁ yaśodāyāṁ nanda-patnyāṁ bhaviṣyasi O all-auspicious Yogamāyā, I shall then appear with my Viṣṇu expansions as the son of Devakī, and you will appear as the daughter of mother Yaśodā, the queen of Mahārāja Nanda. SB 10.2.9 nārāyaṇas tvaṁ na hi sarva-dehinām ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī nārāyaṇo ’ṅgaṁ nara-bhū-jalāyanāt tac cāpi satyaṁ na tavaiva māyā Are you not the original Nārāyaṇa, O supreme controller, since you are the soul of every embodied being and the eternal witness of all created realms? Indeed, Lord Nārāyaṇa is your expansion, and he is called Nārāyaṇa because he is the generating source of the primeval water of the universe. He is real, not a product of your illusory Māyā. SB 10.14.14 yasyāṁśāṁśāṁśa-bhāgena viśvotpatti-layodayāḥ bhavanti kila viśvātmaṁs taṁ tvādyāhaṁ gatiṁ gatā O Soul of all that be, the creation, maintenance and destruction of the universe are all carried out by a fraction of an expansion of an expansion of your expansion. Today I have come to take shelter of you, the Supreme Lord. SB 10.85.31 Though I can to this immediately, when my time energy is engaged to do it, it will take place. It will happen in due time. The word sva (my own) in the phrase sva-kāla-śaktyā is used to indicate that time is also subservient to Kṛṣṇa. You should remain on earth as long as Kṛṣṇa remains visible (as long as he moves on earth). Other than this, he is also eternally performing pastimes in his unmanifest form in Vṛndāvana along with his eternal associates, but he is invisible to others. vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sākaṁ krīḍati mādhavaḥ | vṛndāvanāntaragataḥ sarāmo bālakair vṛtaḥ || Kṛṣṇa plays with the calves and older calves within Vṛndāvana, surrounded by Balarāma and other boys. Skanda Purāṇa rājadhānī tataḥ sābhūt sarva-yādava-bhūbhujām mathurā bhagavān yatra nityaṁ sannihito hariḥ Since that time, the city of Mathurā had been the capital of all the kings of the Yadu dynasty. The city and district of Mathurā are very intimately connected with Kṛṣṇa, for Kṛṣṇa lives there eternally.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa already knows the world's burden — He descends in His own time, and our part is to align as His instruments, not to manage outcomes alone.
    Practical Applications
    • Chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra audibly today, trusting the holy name is non-different from Kṛṣṇa Himself.
    • Notice one news-driven anxiety about the world's chaos and consciously hand it back to the īśvareśvara whose kāla-śakti is already at work.
    • Refuse the modern fantasy that man-made plans alone will fix the world — act in your sva-dharma today as a small aṁśa serving His descent.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where in my life am I assuming Kṛṣṇa is unaware of a burden I am carrying — and what changes the moment I accept that He already knows, before I petition?
    • What 'demoniac' assertion of independence — in my work, my plans, my self-image — am I quietly building, that I would rather diminish myself than have Kṛṣṇa's kāla-śakti diminish for me?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • When a campus or online cause demands you make it your whole identity, remember the Yadu pattern — you can serve a movement as a plenary portion without becoming its protagonist. This week, contribute to one cause without posting about it; let Kṛṣṇa, not the algorithm, be the witness.
    • Notice the urge to 'fix' a struggling friend by managing their feelings, their grades, their relationship. That is material compassion. Real compassion in this verse is bringing them, even once, into the sound of the holy name — share a kīrtan, a verse, a class invite, instead of another pep talk.
    • Before your next exam or interview, pause for sixty seconds and remember puraiva puṁsāvadhṛto — Kṛṣṇa already knows the situation. Your job is sva-dharma effort, not outcome-engineering. Then walk in and work hard.
    householder
    • When the household feels like a burden you alone are carrying — finances, kids' schooling, aging parents — recall that you are a plenary portion in your family's role, not the īśvara of it. Each evening, formally hand the day's unsolved problems to Kṛṣṇa before sleep; pick them up again tomorrow without the false weight of sole proprietorship.
    • In family decisions about money, schools, or career moves, distinguish material compassion (maximizing bodily comfort for the children) from real compassion (giving them sādhana, association, and the holy name). Make at least one decision this month where Kṛṣṇa-conscious upbringing outranks the optimized résumé.
    • Treat your home as a small Yadu-kula — a household whose function is to host Kṛṣṇa, not just to host its members' careers. Establish or strengthen one daily practice the whole family does together: a verse, a chant, prasāda offered before eating.
    senior
    • The dharā-jvara of this age is not yours to cure single-handedly, and at this stage that truth is a relief, not a defeat. Identify one project or worry you have been carrying out of habit and consciously hand it to a younger person — or to Kṛṣṇa — this week.
    • Mentor with the Yadu posture: your role is to prepare plenary portions, not to leave a personal monument. In your conversations with children, grandchildren, and students, speak more of Kṛṣṇa and less of your own accomplishments; let your legacy be their connection to the holy name, not their memory of you.
    • Use the loosening of bodily strength as built-in vairāgya. Each time the body says no to something it once did easily, take it as Kṛṣṇa's sva-kāla-śakti gently diminishing your burden — and increase your chanting by the time freed up.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating Kṛṣṇa's awareness of the earth's distress as a reason for passivity — 'He already knows, so I don't have to act' — instead of recognizing that the demigods were still instructed to take birth and serve as aṁśas.
    • Reading 'kāla-śaktyā kṣapayan' as impersonal cosmic time or karmic mechanism, drifting into an impersonalist frame, when the verse explicitly names Kṛṣṇa as īśvareśvara wielding time as His own potency.
    • Romanticizing the avatāra as a distant historical rescue while ignoring Prabhupāda's purport that the same Kṛṣṇa has appeared now as the Hare Kṛṣṇa name — and so failing to take up nāma-sādhana as the concrete, present-day participation in this very pastime.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Prabhupāda says man-made plans and devices will not bring peace on earth. Pair up and name one specific 'plan' you currently trust to fix the world (political, economic, technological, therapeutic). Where does that trust quietly compete with trust in Kṛṣṇa as īśvareśvaraḥ? Push each other — don't let your partner stop at a pious answer.
    • Brahmā tells the demigods to incarnate as plenary portions in the Yadu family — they get drafted into Kṛṣṇa's mission, not their own. Discuss with your group: when has a 'mission' you wanted to lead been replaced by a smaller supporting role someone else assigned you? Did you treat that as demotion or as service? Where do you still resist being a portion rather than the protagonist?
    • The verse says Kṛṣṇa was already aware of the dharā-jvara before any petition was offered. If He already knows, why pray, why petition, why chant at all? Argue both sides honestly in your pair before settling — and notice if your 'settled' answer is just a slogan you inherited.
    Role Play

    A teacher splits the class into two roles. One student plays a well-meaning activist who has just returned from a climate march, exhausted, convinced that organizing harder is the only real response to the world's burden. The other student plays a Yadu-family member in this verse — someone explicitly told they are being placed on earth as a plenary portion to assist Kṛṣṇa's own descent, not to run their own rescue operation. The activist tries to recruit the Yadu into the cause. The Yadu must respond without dismissing the suffering, without impersonalist platitudes, and without claiming personal heroism — distinguishing real compassion (serving the soul, joining Kṛṣṇa's movement, chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa as Prabhupāda recommends in the purport) from material compassion (treating bodily relief as the final goal). After five minutes, swap roles. Then debrief: where did the Yadu sound preachy? Where did the activist's argument land genuinely?

    Objections & Responses
    • This is just divine outsourcing. 'Kṛṣṇa already knows, Kṛṣṇa will handle it' is exactly the passivity that lets injustice continue. The world's burden gets heavier while devotees chant.
      Read the verse carefully — Kṛṣṇa's awareness does not cancel the demigods' assignment; it shapes it. They are explicitly told to take birth, act, and labor in the Yadu family. Awareness above, action below. The Gauḍīya answer is not passivity but re-located activity: chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, as Prabhupāda says in this very purport, is the actual diminishing of the world's burden, because the burden is finally a burden of forgetfulness, not of logistics. We still feed, still teach, still resist demonic power — but we stop pretending our plans are the prime mover. Sva-kāla-śaktyā — His own time-potency — is the engine. We are limbs.
    • Calling rival nations and their militaries 'demons' is just religious chauvinism dressed up. Every side calls the other side demons. Why should I take Prabhupāda's geopolitical commentary seriously?
      Prabhupāda's category of asura is not ethnic or national — it is defined precisely in BG 16.1 onward, which is in our related-verses list: those who reject the supremacy of the Personality of Godhead and assert independent proprietorship. By that definition, demoniac tendency cuts through every nation, including our own, including ourselves on the days we forget. The verse is not a license to label foreign powers; it is a mirror. Where in my own life do I 'assert myself as independent king and president,' to use Prabhupāda's phrase? That is the asura the chanting actually addresses first. Geopolitics is downstream of that ahaṅkāra.
    Analogy

    Bhagavān knew the earth's distress before anyone reported it — like a father who notices his daughter's silence before she names her sorrow. The verse releases the demigods from the proud illusion that their petition initiated the rescue. Their job is not to inform Him but to participate; they will appear as Kṛṣṇa's sons and grandsons because the cosmic drama needs cast, not because the Director needs reminding.

    Important Words
    • sākṣāt — personally
      Sa + akṣa (eye), 'eye-to-eye, in person.' The verse asserts sākṣāt-bhagavān — not an emanation, not an aṁśa, but Kṛṣṇa Himself. This is the textual anchor for CC Ādi 2 — kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam, Kṛṣṇa is sākṣāt the Person.
    • bhagavān — the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who has full potency
      Used again here in the precise sense: the Person with all six opulences in full. The verse refuses any reading that would reduce Kṛṣṇa to an avatāra or partial expansion. He is the source of avatāras.
    • puruṣaḥ paraḥ — the original person, who is transcendental
      Puruṣaḥ (Person) + paraḥ (highest, transcendental). The Gītā uses paramaḥ puruṣaḥ (15.18) of Kṛṣṇa Himself. Para here distinguishes Him from the other puruṣas (Mahā-Viṣṇu, etc.) — He is the puruṣa above puruṣas.
    • tat-priya-artham — for His satisfaction
      Tat (His) + priya (pleasure, beloved) + artha (purpose). The reason the demigod wives must appear is named directly: His satisfaction. Bhakti's logic — the goal of all activity is Bhagavān's prīti — operates even in cosmic dispatch.
    The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy Him.
    Purport

    In Bhagavad-gītā (4.9) the Lord says, tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti: after giving up the material body, the devotee of the Lord returns home, back to Godhead. This means that the devotee is first transferred to the particular universe where the Lord is at that time staying to exhibit His pastimes. There are innumerable universes, and the Lord is appearing in one of these universes at every moment. Therefore His pastimes are called nitya-līlā, eternal pastimes. The Lord’s appearance as a child in the house of Devakī takes place continuously in one universe after another. Therefore, the devotee is first transferred to that particular universe where the pastimes of the Lord are current. As stated in Bhagavad-gītā, even if a devotee does not complete the course of devotional service, he enjoys the happiness of the heavenly planets, where the most pious people dwell, and then takes birth in the house of a śuci or śrīmān, a pious brāhmaṇa or a wealthy vaiśya ( śucīnāṁ śrīmatāṁ gehe yoga-bhraṣṭo ’bhijāyate ). Thus a pure devotee, even if unable to execute devotional service completely, is transferred to the upper planetary system, where pious people reside. From there, if his devotional service is complete, such a devotee is transferred to the place where the Lord’s pastimes are going on. Herein it is said, sambhavantu sura-striyaḥ. Sura-strī, the women of the heavenly planets, were thus ordered to appear in the Yadu dynasty in Vṛndāvana to enrich the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. These sura-strī, when further trained to live with Kṛṣṇa, would be transferred to the original Goloka Vṛndāvana. During Lord Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes within this world, the sura-strī were to appear in different ways in different families to give pleasure to the Lord, just so that they would be fully trained before going to the eternal Goloka Vṛndāvana. With the association of Lord Kṛṣṇa, either at Dvārakā-purī, Mathurā-purī or Vṛndāvana, they would certainly return home, back to Godhead. Among the sura-strī, the women of the heavenly planets, there are many devotees, such as the mother of the Upendra incarnation of Kṛṣṇa. It was such devoted women who were called for in this connection.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy Him.
    Commentary

    Sura striya, the wives of the devas, refers to expansions of Krsna’s eternal female companions, who were present in the heavenly planets. Examples are the wives of the manvatara avataras such as Upendra or Vamana. They performed worship to attain friendship and intimacy with Krsna’s most dear lovers. Because of this worship they should take birth in different forms as priya sakhis of Krsna. In the Ujjvala nilamani it is said: nitya priyanam amsas tu -When Krsna appears in the family of the devas in partial form, his beloveds also appear as the forms of devis to please him. When Krsna appeared on earth, they took the form of young unmarried gopis, as priya sakhis of the nitya priya sakhis.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having mentioned that Kṛṣṇa is the source of all forms of God, Viṣṇu now describes the esoteric goal of Svayam Bhagavān’s appearance: his blissful pastimes. Kṛṣṇa is described as puruṣaḥ paraḥ, the person to whom no one is superior, and as Bhagavān, endowed with all powers. By mentioning this, no one can say he is born like an ordinary jīva. He will appear (rather than be born) personally in Vasudeva’s house. In order to please him (tat-priyārtham) by your service, or in order to serve his dear consorts such as Rukmiṇī and Rādhā (tat-priyā), the wives of the devatās should make their appearance in the best possible way (sambhavantu). Or they should become qualified (sambhavantu). This means the Lord would bless them with suitable qualification and they would then appear.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa Himself descends as Vasudeva's son in eternal nitya-līlā — even sura-strīs are summoned to serve Him; nothing matters but readiness for His pastimes.
    Practical Applications
    • Today, refuse the impersonalist drift in your thinking — speak of Kṛṣṇa by name as a Person, not as 'the divine' or 'consciousness.'
    • Take one concrete step in sādhana that prepares you for direct service — chant attentively, hear one verse, or render a small kāya-vāk-manas offering before sleep.
    • Notice one comfort or status you are quietly attached to, and consciously offer it to Kṛṣṇa as belonging to Him, not to your enjoyment.
    Reflection Questions
    • This verse shows that even the sura-strī, residents of the heavenly planets, had to take birth in a particular family at a particular time to be 'fully trained' before going to Goloka — where am I treating my present circumstances (this family, this stage, this duty) as an obstacle to bhakti rather than as the precise training ground Kṛṣṇa has arranged for me?
    • Prabhupāda says the Lord's pastimes are nitya-līlā, going on continuously in some universe at every moment — what would change in how I read Kṛṣṇa's līlā, and how I sit for sādhana today, if I stopped relating to it as ancient history and started relating to it as something happening right now?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • When you scroll today, notice how every feed is engineered to make YOU the one being satisfied — likes, validation, dopamine. Flip it once: spend ten minutes chanting or reading SB with the explicit intention 'this is to please Kṛṣṇa, not to make me feel spiritual.' Watch how strange and uncomfortable that is — that discomfort is the whole curriculum.
    • You are at the age where peer groups are forming around 'who you are becoming.' The sura-strīs were called down by name for a specific service. Pick ONE friendship or group where you are quietly performing for approval, and ask yourself: if Kṛṣṇa were the audience instead of these people, would I still say what I'm saying? Don't ghost the friends — change the audience in your own head.
    • Exam season makes you bargain with God: 'let me pass and I'll be devotional after.' This verse says the opposite — devotional service is not the reward you earn after success, it is the training that makes you fit for Kṛṣṇa's association. Today, do fifteen minutes of japa or śāstra-study BEFORE you study, with no transactional expectation, and let your studies be the offering, not the bribe.
    householder
    • Your spouse, your kids, your career — all of it is your current 'universe' where Kṛṣṇa's pastimes can be entered through sva-dharma. Stop waiting for a future renunciation. This week, identify one decision (a job change, a school for the child, a money question) you have been making for your own satisfaction and re-decide it asking 'what does this look like as service?' — not as a slogan, but with the actual numbers and tradeoffs on the table.
    • Prabhupāda's purport says the yoga-bhraṣṭa takes birth in a śuci or śrīmān family. If you are a householder reading this, that is likely YOU — you got the human birth, the means, the access to śāstra. The question is no longer whether you were given the opportunity. It is whether your children will inherit a home where Kṛṣṇa is the center, or just a home where Kṛṣṇa is mentioned. Pick one daily family practice — ārati, a verse at dinner, a Sunday program — and install it this week, not next month.
    • Money and time are the two currencies a householder fights over. The sura-strīs were called for a specific service, not for general piety. Audit one month of your spending and one week of your calendar, and ask: what fraction is going to viṣaya (sense gratification dressed up as 'family needs') versus actual service? Don't moralize the answer — just see it clearly, and shift one line item.
    senior
    • You are closer to the body's transition than the youth in the room, and this verse is a direct mercy for you: the devotee does not lose the pastimes by dying — he is transferred to the universe where they are currently happening. Today, write down what you are still afraid to lose at death. Read the list. Then read the verse. Notice which fears the verse actually answers and which are just ahaṅkāra clinging.
    • Mentoring is your sva-dharma now, but the modern temptation is to mentor for legacy — 'so they remember me.' The sura-strīs were called to satisfy Kṛṣṇa, not to be remembered. Pick one younger person — a grandchild, a junior devotee, a neighbor — and give them one hour this week of undivided attention with no agenda of being thanked or quoted later. Let the service be the whole point.
    • Loosen one attachment this month, deliberately. Not the easy ones (a possession you were already tired of) — a real one: a grudge you have nursed for decades, a role in the family you refuse to let your children take over, a self-image as 'the one who knows.' Offer it specifically to Kṛṣṇa. Santoṣa at this stage is not passive contentment; it is the active letting-go that makes you light enough to be transferred when the time comes.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Reading 'sura-strī were called to enrich Kṛṣṇa's pastimes' as a license for sentimental fantasy about being a gopī or playmate of the Lord, instead of doing the unglamorous training the present āśrama actually demands.
    • Concluding from 'even yoga-bhraṣṭas are transferred to pious families' that one can coast on partial sādhana — turning the verse's mercy into an excuse to slacken viṣaya-tyāga and daily sādhana now.
    • Slipping into impersonalist drift by treating 'returning home, back to Godhead' as merger or a state of consciousness, when the verse is explicitly about a personal Kṛṣṇa appearing in a specific house, in a specific dynasty, with specific associates.
    Discussion Prompts
    • The verse says the sura-strīs were called down specifically to please Kṛṣṇa — not for their own enjoyment or fulfillment. Where in your own sādhana do you secretly want to be 'called' for your own pleasure rather than for His? Share one place where this self-deception is operating right now.
    • Prabhupāda's purport claims that even an incomplete devotee enjoys the heavenly planets first and then takes birth in a śuci or śrīmān family. Does this sound like a consolation prize that lets us slack off, or like a serious warning about the cost of incompletion? Defend your reading against the opposite view in the room.
    • The pastimes are nitya-līlā — happening continuously in some universe at every moment. If this is literally true, what does it change about your day today? If it sounds mythological to you, name the specific resistance — and let someone in the group push back on it without being polite.
    Role Play

    Two students pair up. Student A is a long-time devotee who has just been told by a senior Vaiṣṇava that, because their sādhana is incomplete, they will likely 'go to the heavenly planets first' rather than directly to Goloka. Student A is unsettled — it sounds like failure. Student B is a fellow practitioner who has read this verse and its purport. B's job, in five minutes, is NOT to comfort A with vague reassurance but to honestly help A see (a) that the arrangement is Kṛṣṇa's mercy, not punishment, (b) what concretely is missing from A's sādhana right now, and (c) one specific thing A can do this week to close that gap. Then swap roles. Debrief: where did the conversation drift into material consolation instead of real compassion?

    Objections & Responses
    • Calling down 'wives of the demigods' to satisfy Kṛṣṇa sounds patriarchal and instrumentalizing — women as ornaments for a male deity's pastimes. Why should a modern reader take this seriously?
      The framing inverts the modern reading. The sura-strīs are not being used; they are being given the rarest opportunity in all the universes — direct association with the Supreme Personality of Godhead, training that culminates in eternal Goloka Vṛndāvana. In our material conditioning, 'satisfying another' sounds like degradation because we project our own exploitative relationships onto it. But in the spiritual realm, satisfying Kṛṣṇa IS the soul's own highest fulfillment — there is no split between His pleasure and the devotee's. The sura-strīs are advanced devotees from the heavenly planets being promoted, not commodities being deployed. The 'patriarchy' lens is a category error: it imports a material power-relation into a domain where Kṛṣṇa is not a 'male' in the bodily sense and the devotees are not 'females' in the bodily sense — both are eternal souls, and the rasa is svarūpa-based, not gender-political.
    • Innumerable universes, the Lord appearing in one of them every moment, eternal pastimes running in parallel — this is mythology dressed up as cosmology. A serious adult shouldn't need to believe this to live a moral life.
      Two responses, and the second is the one that actually matters. First: the 'serious adult' claim assumes the modern materialist cosmology is the neutral default and śāstra is the optional ornament. But that cosmology is itself a metaphysical commitment — one that cannot account for consciousness, for the persistence of the self, or for why moral life should bind us at all. Second, and more important: the verse is not asking you to assent to a cosmological diagram. It is telling you that Kṛṣṇa's pastimes are not a one-time historical event you missed by 5,000 years — they are eternally available, and a devotee whose sādhana ripens enters them. That is not mythology; that is the practical promise the whole tradition rests on. If you find yourself needing the cosmology to be 'symbolic' before you can practice, ask honestly whether you are protecting your modern self-image or seriously testing the claim. The Gauḍīya answer is: chant, hear, serve — and the cosmology will stop feeling like a hurdle and start feeling like a description of where you actually are.
    Analogy

    Kṛṣṇa will appear as Vasudeva's son — not as a borrowed body, not as a partial expansion, but personally, sākṣāt. The demigods' wives are dispatched to take birth as the women who will serve Him. The line of preparation is precise: where the Person Himself comes, the supporting cast must be in place beforehand. Yoga-māyā is the casting director.

    Important Words
    • vāsudeva-kalā anantaḥ — the plenary expansion of Lord Kṛṣṇa known as Anantadeva or Saṅkarṣaṇa Ananta
      Vāsudeva-kalā = a portion of Vāsudeva; Ananta = endless. The same Person who is the infinite serpent-bed of Mahā-Viṣṇu now appears as a child. Gauḍīya theology: the infinite voluntarily takes finite form to serve mādhurya.
    • sahasra-vadanaḥ — having thousands of hoods
      Sahasra (thousand) + vadana (mouth/face). Ananta-Śeṣa's cosmic form has thousands of hoods on which the universes rest. The same Person — whose hoods bear the worlds — will be wrestled by Kṛṣṇa's playmates in Vraja.
    • svarāṭ — fully independent
      Sva (own) + rāj (ruler) — 'self-ruling.' Used in the Bhāgavata's first verse (janmādy asya yataḥ ... svarāṭ) of the Absolute. Saṅkarṣaṇa is svarāṭ — independent in Himself — yet voluntarily subordinates Himself in līlā as Balarāma. Independence used for service.
    • priya-cikīrṣayā — with the desire to act for the pleasure
      Priya (beloved, pleasure) + cikīrṣā (desire to do; from kṛ). The whole motive of Balarāma's appearance is named: to do what pleases Kṛṣṇa. The eternal servant-mood (dāsya) coloring even sakhya-rasa with Kṛṣṇa.
    The foremost manifestation of Kṛṣṇa is Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is known as Ananta. He is the origin of all incarnations within this material world. Previous to the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa, this original Saṅkarṣaṇa will appear as Baladeva, just to please the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa in His transcendental pastimes.
    Purport

    Śrī Baladeva is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself. He is equal in supremacy to the Supreme Godhead, yet wherever Kṛṣṇa appears, Śrī Baladeva appears as His brother, sometimes elder and sometimes younger. When Kṛṣṇa appears, all His plenary expansions and other incarnations appear with Him. This is elaborately explained in Caitanya-caritāmṛta. This time, Baladeva would appear before Kṛṣṇa as Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The foremost manifestation of Kṛṣṇa is Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is known as Ananta. He is the origin of all incarnations within this material world. Previous to the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa, this original Saṅkarṣaṇa will appear as Baladeva, just to please the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa in His transcendental pastimes.
    Commentary

    Svarat usually means independent, he who exists (raj or rat) by himself (sva), but here it means he who exists with his own brother Krsna (sva). Baladeva (deva) who is existing with his own brother (svarat) will appear first (agratah bhavita). Ananta is an amsa or kala of Baladeva. This is supported with verses like: evamsena sahasra vadano’nantah (whose portion is the thousand mouthed ananta) and yasaikamsena vidhrta jagati jagatah pateh ( O mighty armed balarama, Who by one portion supports the universe.) Here Baladeva is described as Ananta who is a portion of Vasudeva.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    His elder brother will appear first. His brother’s qualifications are described. Vāsudeva refers to Kṛṣṇa as part of the caturvyūha in Dvārakā. His kalā or expansion there is Saṅkarśaṇa. He is unlimited (anantaḥ) and has a thousand heads as the expansion Śeṣa in order to praise the qualities of Kṛṣṇa. āma rāma mahā-bāho na jāne tava vikramam yasyaikāṁśena vidhṛtā jagatī jagataḥ pate Rāma, Rāma, O mighty-armed one! I know nothing of your prowess. With a single portion of yourself you hold up the earth, O Lord of the universe. SB 10.65.28 The “single portion of yourself” refers to Śeṣa. Svarāṭ means he who exists (rājate) with Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa, the highest svarūpa (sva). This means that he does not exist without Kṛṣṇa. He is called deva because he is to be worshipped by all, since he is Svayam Bhagavān’s elder brother. “But he should be the younger brother of Svayam Bhagavān like Lakṣmaṇa, the younger brother of Rāma.” He takes this role of an older brother to please Kṛṣṇa. Being able to destroy the Lord’s pain by being obedient and at the same time an equal, he has a special friendly relationship with Kṛṣṇa as his devotee. In the Bṛhad-sahasra-nāma-stotra, among the names of Balarāma there is pūrva-bhakti-khedācyutāgrajaḥ: he became the elder brother of the Lord because of Lord’s pain in previous pastimes of Rāma. In those previous pastimes he could not relieve Rāma of distress because he was younger. This means that in some kalpas he does not appear in a dependant position. Since Lakṣmaṇa is dependent, he cannot freely remove Rāma’s distress. “Being elder, I desire to give him happiness independently.” Thus Lakṣmaṇa laments in devotion, because he is not able to relieve the Lord’ pain. He desired to give happiness to Hari, out of affection since Hari is most attractive. Thus he appears as the elder brother.

    Personal Guidance
    Baladeva, Kṛṣṇa's own first expansion as Saṅkarṣaṇa-Ananta, descends as elder brother solely for hareḥ priya-cikīrṣayā — to please Kṛṣṇa.
    Practical Applications
    • Begin one task today with the explicit motive 'to please Kṛṣṇa,' and notice how it reorders your priorities mid-stream.
    • Speak to your elder brother, sister, or senior with the awareness that their service is itself a form of Baladeva-tattva — assist them rather than compete.
    • Refuse the impersonalist reflex that flattens Kṛṣṇa into 'the divine'; address Him by name in your japa today and feel the personal relation.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where in my life am I trying to stand alone in service to Kṛṣṇa, when this verse shows that even the Lord's own expansion appears first to support His pastimes — whose accompanying service have I been refusing to recognize?
    • Baladeva descends only hareḥ priya-cikīrṣayā — solely to please Kṛṣṇa. When I examine my own sādhana today, what subtle second motive (recognition, peace of mind, advancement) is competing with that single purpose?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • Identify one friend or sibling whose success you secretly compete with on social media. For one week, deliberately act in priya-cikīrṣayā toward them — promote their work, show up for their thing, without posting about your own role in it. Notice the ahaṅkāra that resists.
    • In your next group project or study circle, take the Baladeva position on purpose: be the elder-brother figure who clears the path for someone else to shine, even if you could have led. Journal what shifted in your motivation by the end of the week.
    • When a peer 'beats' you — better grade, better internship, better relationship — practice the dhīra response: 'Kṛṣṇa is acting through that result; my role is right action and to please Him, not to be the star.' Catch yourself the moment envy starts and re-aim there.
    householder
    • In one family decision this week (school, money, where to spend a weekend), consciously yield your preference to your spouse's or child's flourishing — not as suppression, but as priya-cikīrṣayā. At day's end, offer the yielding to Kṛṣṇa rather than banking it as a grievance.
    • Examine your career ambition: where are you the protagonist demanding to be Kṛṣṇa, and where could you be the Baladeva — the one who quietly makes another's success possible (a colleague, a younger sibling, your own children)? Pick one such relationship and recommit to it for the next quarter.
    • Read SB 10.1.24 with your spouse or older child this week. Discuss together: what would it mean for our household if we treated one another's flourishing as the form of our own service to Kṛṣṇa, rather than as a transaction?
    senior
    • You are nearer to the role Baladeva models — the elder who appears 'before' the younger to prepare the ground. Identify one younger person (child, grandchild, junior at the temple) whose path you can clear without asking for credit, and commit to a concrete act of clearing this month.
    • Audit the attachments you are still holding to being the central figure — in family decisions, in inheritance, in who is consulted first. Loosen one this week as an offering: step back deliberately so a younger person can step forward, in the mood of priya-cikīrṣayā.
    • Use this verse as a meditation on your own approaching transition. Just as Baladeva appears 'before' Kṛṣṇa to please Him, you are now the senior making space for what comes next. Each evening, offer the day — its diminishments included — to Kṛṣṇa, asking only that your remaining time be spent pleasing Him through serving His devotees.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating Baladeva as a lesser or secondary deity rather than as the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself appearing in the mood of a servitor — the verse establishes equality in supremacy, with difference only in līlā-rasa.
    • Reading 'Ananta,' 'Saṅkarṣaṇa,' and 'Baladeva' as separate or competing identities and getting lost in cataloging expansions, instead of seeing the one personal Lord serving Kṛṣṇa's pastimes — drifting into impersonal or merely scholastic study (failed svādhyāya).
    • Romanticizing the 'elder brother who serves the younger' as a sentimental image while ignoring its concrete demand: that real anahaṅkāra means voluntarily taking the supporting role in one's own family, saṅga, or work today, not merely admiring it in the līlā.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Baladeva appears as Kṛṣṇa's elder brother purely to please Him — share with your partner one relationship in your life where you genuinely subordinate your preference to another's pleasure, and one where you only pretend to. What is the actual difference you feel inside?
    • The verse says Saṅkarṣaṇa is 'equal in supremacy' to Kṛṣṇa yet takes the role of servitor-brother. Does this strike you as inspiring or troubling? Argue the case that voluntary subordination is higher than mutual equality, and let someone in the group push back honestly.
    • Where in modern life — career, parenting, sādhana — do we confuse 'being the protagonist of my own story' with svadhyāya, and where does Baladeva's example of priya-cikīrṣayā (acting only to please another) cut against that instinct? Bring a concrete example, not a theory.
    Role Play

    Two students pair up. Student A is the older sibling who has just been told by their parents that the family is moving cities so the younger sibling (Student B) can attend a specialized program — A's own college plans, friend group, and a relationship will all be disrupted. Student B did not ask for this and feels guilty. Run the conversation twice: first, A speaks from ahaṅkāra ('I'm sacrificing everything for you') — notice how it lands. Second, A speaks in the mood of priya-cikīrṣayā — wanting the younger one's flourishing, with no ledger. The group then debriefs: what was different in the body, the tone, the silence afterward? Where did each of you feel the pull back to ahaṅkāra?

    Objections & Responses
    • This is just mythology dressed up as theology — one God 'expanding' into a brother to play with Himself sounds like a fairy tale, not something a serious adult should organize their life around.
      The objection assumes the standard of 'serious' is impersonal abstraction — a featureless Absolute, or no God at all. The Gauḍīya line answers that the highest reality is not less personal than us but infinitely more so. A God who can expand into a brother, a friend, a beloved — without diminishment — is philosophically richer than a static One, because it accounts for relationship as ultimate, not derivative. Baladeva is not Kṛṣṇa playing with a mirror; He is the eternal Other through whom Kṛṣṇa's sweetness is tasted. Try the experiment from the inside: live one week as if your relationships are the stage on which the Supreme is rehearsing His own līlā, and see whether 'fairy tale' or 'serious adult' feels truer.
    • If Baladeva is Himself the Supreme Personality of Godhead, why would He 'serve' Kṛṣṇa? Doesn't this just create a hierarchy inside God — and isn't the Advaitin view (one undifferentiated Absolute) cleaner?
      Cleaner, yes — and emptier. The Advaitin solution dissolves the lover and the beloved into a single substance, and with them dissolves prema, bhakti, and every relationship that gives life its taste. The Gauḍīya answer is that Baladeva's 'service' is not subordination imposed from outside; it is the internal structure of love itself, where the lover wishes only the beloved's pleasure (priya-cikīrṣayā) and the beloved is magnified, not diminished, by being loved. Within Godhead this is eternal, voluntary, and mutually full. Hierarchy here is not a defect to be smoothed away — it is the very shape of rasa. Remove it and you do not get a higher truth; you get a sterile one.
    Analogy

    Saṅkarṣaṇa Ananta will appear as Balarāma before Kṛṣṇa — like the elder brother walking into the wedding hall first to ensure the seating, before the groom arrives. He goes ahead not because he is greater but because his service is to make the Lord's appearance comfortable. The eternal brother-servant has already entered before the curtain rises.

    Important Words
    • viṣṇoḥ māyā — the potency of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu
      Viṣṇu's māyā — His own internal potency, not the deluding material māyā that traps the jīva. The Gauḍīya distinction is fundamental: there is yoga-māyā (internal, attendant on the Lord) and mahā-māyā (external, governing matter). Both are His.
    • bhagavatī — as good as Bhagavān and therefore known as Bhagavatī
      Feminine of bhagavān. Because the Lord's potency shares His nature non-differentially, she carries His name. Acintya-bhedābheda visible: she is His and yet a person — both, by the same logic that holds for Rādhā.
    • sammohitam — captivated
      Past participle of sam-muh, 'completely deluded.' Yoga-māyā's function: she conceals Kṛṣṇa's full opulence so that intimate līlā is possible. The cowherds 'don't know' He is Bhagavān not because they lack information but because yoga-māyā lovingly hides it.
    • ādiṣṭā — being ordered
      Past participle of ā-diś, 'to direct, command.' Yoga-māyā operates only on the Lord's command. She is never an autonomous goddess; her every act is a direct execution of His will. The verse establishes hierarchy: His command, her execution.
    The potency of the Lord, known as viṣṇu-māyā, who is as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will also appear with Lord Kṛṣṇa. This potency, acting in different capacities, captivates all the worlds, both material and spiritual. At the request of her master, she will appear with her different potencies in order to execute the work of the Lord.
    Purport

    Parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate ( Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 6.8). In the Vedas it is said that the potencies of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are called by different names, such as yoga-māyā and mahā-māyā. Ultimately, however, the Lord’s potency is one, exactly as electric potency is one although it can act both to cool and to heat. The Lord’s potency acts in both the spiritual and material worlds. In the spiritual world the Lord’s potency works as yoga-māyā, and in the material world the same potency works as mahā-māyā, exactly as electricity works in both a heater and a cooler. In the material world, this potency, working as mahā-māyā, acts upon the conditioned souls to deprive them more and more of devotional service. It is said, yayā sammohito jīva ātmānaṁ tri-guṇātmakam. In the material world the conditioned soul thinks of himself as a product of tri-guṇa, the three modes of material nature. This is the bodily conception of life. Because of associating with the three guṇas of the material potency, everyone identifies himself with his body. Someone is thinking he is a brāhmaṇa, someone a kṣatriya, and someone a vaiśya or śūdra. Actually, however, one is neither a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya nor a śūdra; one is part and parcel of the Supreme Lord ( mamaivāṁśaḥ ), but because of being covered by the material energy, mahā-māyā, one identifies himself in these different ways. When the conditioned soul becomes liberated, however, he thinks himself an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa. Jīvera ‘svarūpa’ haya-kṛṣṇera ‘nitya-dāsa . ’ When he comes to that position, the same potency, acting as yoga-māyā, increasingly helps him become purified and devote his energy to the service of the Lord. In either case, whether the soul is conditioned or liberated, the Lord is supreme. As stated in Bhagavad-gītā (9.10) , mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-carācaram: it is by the order of the Supreme Personality of Godhead that the material energy, mahā-māyā, works upon the conditioned soul. prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate “The bewildered spirit soul, under the influence of the three modes of material nature, thinks himself to be the doer of activities which are in actuality carried out by nature.” ( Bg. 3.27 ) Within conditioned life, no one has freedom, but because one is bewildered, being subject to the rule of mahā-māyā, one foolishly thinks himself independent ( ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate ). But when the conditioned soul becomes liberated by executing devotional service, he is given a greater and greater chance to relish a relationship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead in different transcendental statuses, such as dāsya-rasa, sakhya-rasa, vātsalya-rasa and mādhurya-rasa. Thus the Lord’s potency, viṣṇu-māyā, has two features: āvaraṇikā and unmukha. When the Lord appeared, His potency came with Him and acted in different ways. She acted as Yoga-māyā with Yaśodā, Devakī and other intimate relations of the Lord, and she acted in a different way with Kaṁsa, Śālva and other asuras. By the order of Lord Kṛṣṇa, His potency Yoga-māyā came with Him and exhibited different activities according to the time and circumstances ( kāryārthe sambhaviṣyati ). Yoga-māyā acted differently to execute different purposes desired by the Lord. As confirmed in Bhagavad-gītā (9.13) , mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ. The mahātmās, who fully surrender to the lotus feet of the Lord, are directed by Yoga-māyā, whereas the durātmās, those who are devoid of devotional service, are directed by Mahā-māyā.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The potency of the Lord, known as viṣṇu-māyā, who is as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will also appear with Lord Kṛṣṇa. This potency, acting in different capacities, captivates all the worlds, both material and spiritual. At the request of her master, she will appear with her different potencies in order to execute the work of the Lord.
    Commentary

    In order to charm the eternal devotees and bewilder the enemies like Kamsa, he gave orders to Yogamaya and Mayadevi. Here the word visnor maya refers to both energies of the Lord but elsewhere in Bhagavatam it is stated that he gave orders to yoga maya. Being ordered by the Lord, yogamaya, along with her expansion, the external energy (amsena), which bewilders the world, will appear. Or the meaning youga maya will appear with mahamaya, by which the spiritual and material worlds are bewildered. That maya is an expansion of yogamaya is stated in the sruti vidya conversation in Narada Pancaratra. "Yogamaya, who is the svarupa sakti of Visnu, knowledge of whom bestows instant attainment of the Lord, who is unswerving in devotion to the Lord, surrendered completely to the Lord, whose nature is prema, rules over Gokula like a queen. By her mercy very easily one can attain the Lord. Her avarika sakti is Mahamaya, the controller of the material realm. By her influence all the jivas identify with their bodies and become bewildered." Another name of this Durga is eka, or ekanamsa. They will appear for the purpose of activities. (karyarthe) There are two types of activities: those of yoga maya and those of maya. It was Yogamaya who took the seventh child from Devaki’s womb, came to the prison where Krsna was born and put Yasoda into deep sleep to exchange the children. These are activities of Yogamaya, not Mahamaya. Mahamaya does not have the power to transfer her master Balarama to another womb. Yasoda’s sleep is not the work of mahamaya because the scriptures say: beyond the fourth state of consciousness is the fifth state of prema. This is the state of dreaming of the associates of Hari. Their sleep and dreaming do not arise through the modes of nature. Maha maya cannot extend her power to the eternal devotees of the Lord. The form of Devaki’s daughter to be killed by Kamsa was mahamaya, not yogamaya. Yoga maya does not involve herself with such sinful people. Mahamaya slipped from Kamsa’s hands and rose up in the sky, settled in many places with many names. She herself said: I will be born from the womb of Yasoda in Nanda’s house in the twenty eighth yuga cycle at the end of vaivasvata manvantara. As the dweller of the vindya mountains, I will kill your evil companions. " The bewilderment of the husbands and mothers-in-law of the married gopis in performing the rasa lila is an action of yogamaya , not maya, because the husbands are not unfavorable towards the Lord or atheistic. If they were under the influence of maya, then one would certainly observe in them hostility towards the Lord. In the first verse at the beginning of the description of the rasa lila, the words " yogamayam upasrita" are used. On the other hand, demons like Duryodhana and Salva, though they see the Lord’s visvarupa and Garuda, they never give respect to the Lord. They think he is one of the wicked Yadavas. This is the action of maya, not yogamaya, because one can see in their actions hostility to the Lord. Bewilderment of those hostile to the Lord is the action of maya and bewilderment of the devotee is the action of yogamaya. When Yasoda saw Krsna’s visvarupa in his mouth, , and when Nanda saw Krsna in Varunaloka, because of their extreme affection as parents, though they saw reverential aspects of the Lord, they were completely unaffected by it. This is neither the action of yogamaya, nor maya. It is the nature of prema itself. This prema covers up knowledge of the Lord’s powers, and with the ropes of spiritual possessiveness, binds up Krsna in their hearts more and more. With this increase in affection for the Lord, prema drowns the devotees completely in the great ocean of relishing the sweetness of Krsna. To convey this unique quality of prema, the tantra says: "Krsna spread his vaisnavi maya in the form of parental affection." Extreme affection for a son is the unique quality of vatsalya prema. In this verse yoga maya is referred to as "maya" since it shares the quality of spreading illusion with mahamaya.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Māyā is the śakti of Bhagavān who pervades the universe (viṣṇoḥ). She is called bhagavatī because she is endowed with all powers. She is then shown as bhagavatī by describing her specific actions. She bewilders the world. This function is completely different from the cic-cakti. She will appear completely by the will of the Lord. Without the Lord’s will, she is unable to bewilder Yaśodā and others. Because bewildering Yaśodā is most confidential, that is not stated directly here: she appears for certain activities (kāryārthe). “We devatās are your unlimited order-carriers and will appear to please the Lord. Yaśodā is completely independent. How can māyā bewilder her?” She has been directly ordered by Kṛṣṇa, her master. “You have said she bewilders the world. When she takes birth she will bewilder us also.” She will act as an aṁśa, following Kṛṣṇa’s will. She will bewilder according to his desire alone.

    Personal Guidance
    Kṛṣṇa's potency viṣṇu-māyā has two faces — āvaraṇikā that bewilders the conditioned and unmukhā (yoga-māyā) that uncovers Him for the surrendered.
    Practical Applications
    • Notice each time today you say 'I am' followed by a bodily or social label (brāhmaṇa, professional, parent) and silently correct it to 'I am Kṛṣṇa's eternal servant'.
    • Refuse the ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha thought 'I am the doer' when a task succeeds or fails — verbally offer the result to Kṛṣṇa so the same potency turns from covering to revealing.
    • Speak to one āvaraṇikā-bound soul today — not to fix their body's discomfort, but to plant one word about Kṛṣṇa that invites yoga-māyā's mercy.
    Reflection Questions
    • In which areas of my life am I still acting as the ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā — convinced I am the doer — when in fact viṣṇu-māyā is arranging the outcome behind my efforts?
    • Where am I currently being directed by māyā in her āvaraṇikā (covering) mode — keeping me identified with body, varṇa, or role — and what one act of devotional service today would invite the unmukha (revealing, yoga-māyā) face of the same potency to act on me instead?
    For Each Age Group
    youth
    • When you scroll Instagram tonight and feel that familiar pull — that you ARE your follower count, your grades, your friend group's approval — name it out loud as mahā-māyā's āvaraṇikā feature covering you. Don't fight it; just see it. The seeing itself is yoga-māyā beginning to turn you.
    • Pick one identity you have been performing this semester — 'I'm the smart one,' 'I'm the chill one,' 'I'm the rebel,' 'I'm the spiritual one in my friend group' — and for one full day, refuse to perform it. Notice how strongly the false ego protests. That protest is your evidence the Gītā is describing you, not someone in 5000 BCE.
    • Before your next exam or interview, formally request: 'Kṛṣṇa, let Your potency act on me as yoga-māyā today, not mahā-māyā. I am not the doer; I am Your part and parcel doing my work as offering.' Then study or prepare harder than ever — the prayer is not a substitute for effort, it is the orientation of the effort.
    householder
    • In your next family financial decision — the school choice, the car, the renovation — explicitly ask before deciding: is this choice being made by ahaṅkāra (the 'I'm the provider, I decide' false ego) or as a servant of Kṛṣṇa caring for souls He has placed in your charge? Same action, two potencies. Choose the second.
    • Your children are being shaped by mahā-māyā every hour through screens, schools, and peer culture that tell them they are their bodies, their grades, their identities. Your one non-negotiable household duty is to introduce yoga-māyā into the home — a daily ārati, a meal offered, a verse read at bedtime — so that the same potency can begin to turn them. Start this week, not next year.
    • When your spouse irritates you tonight, catch the exact moment your mind labels them with their body-identity ('he always,' 'she never,' 'typical of her family'). That labeling is mahā-māyā at work in YOUR consciousness, not theirs. Drop the label, see the eternal soul Kṛṣṇa has given you to serve, and respond from that vision.
    senior
    • You have spent decades accumulating identities — professional title, parental role, community standing, even devotee reputation. The body is now visibly returning these. Don't grieve the loss; recognize it as Kṛṣṇa's mercy stripping the āvaraṇikā covering so that yoga-māyā has clearer ground to work. Each thing taken is a veil lifted.
    • Mentor at least one younger person this month not by transferring your professional expertise but by transmitting what you have learned about the difference between mahā-māyā and yoga-māyā in your own life. Specific failures, specific turnings. Your accumulated discrimination (viveka) is the legacy that matters; everything else is ash.
    • Each night before sleep, rehearse leaving the body the way the verse describes the soul as Kṛṣṇa's part and parcel (mamaivāṁśaḥ). Withdraw consciously from the bodily identification — 'I am not this body, this name, this résumé' — and place yourself, by His grace, under yoga-māyā's care for the night. Practice the final departure now, in small nightly rehearsals, so it is not a stranger when it comes.
    Common Pitfalls
    • Treating yoga-māyā and mahā-māyā as two separate goddesses or warring forces, instead of one potency of Kṛṣṇa acting in two directions — and so falling into a quasi-dualistic, demigod-style worship rather than recognizing every movement of energy as His arrangement.
    • Using 'it's all māyā' as a fatalistic shrug — excusing passivity, neglect of sva-dharma, or refusal to act — when the verse's whole point is that the same potency comes to execute the Lord's work (kāryārthe sambhaviṣyati), which means the devotee is meant to engage, not withdraw.
    • Drifting into impersonalist language — 'merge with the energy,' 'awaken the Self,' 'feel the divine within' — and forgetting that viṣṇu-māyā is ādiṣṭā prabhuṇā, dispatched by a Person, and that liberation here means becoming Kṛṣṇa's nitya-dāsa, not dissolving into an abstract Absolute.
    Discussion Prompts
    • Prabhupāda says the same potency acts as yoga-māyā for devotees and mahā-māyā for asuras — like one electricity heating or cooling. Where in your own life have you seen the SAME circumstance (a job loss, a relationship rupture, an illness) push one person deeper into Kṛṣṇa and another deeper into bewilderment? What made the difference, and which way is it pulling you right now? Disagree honestly with your partner if you think the difference is just temperament, not the Lord's arrangement.
    • The verse says māyā 'captivates all the worlds.' Pick the one identity you cling to most — brāhmaṇa-by-temperament, professional, parent, intellectual, spiritual seeker — and argue why it is NOT māyā. Then let your partner argue why it is. Don't settle for a polite synthesis.
    • Prabhupāda contrasts āvaraṇikā (covering) and unmukha (turning toward) features of viṣṇu-māyā. Name one specific area of your life where māyā is currently covering you (you are bewildered and don't see it as bewilderment) and one where she is turning you toward Kṛṣṇa. How do you tell the two apart in real time, not in retrospect?
    Role Play

    Two students are assigned roles. Student A is a successful 35-year-old software engineer who has just been promoted and is celebrating. Student B is a fellow devotee who knows that Student A has been skipping morning sādhana for three months because of work pressure, and has started saying things like 'I'm just wired this way — I'm a builder, a kṣatriya at heart.' B's task: in a five-minute conversation over chai, gently challenge A to see that the 'I am a builder' identity is exactly the ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate the Gītā warns about — without being preachy, without quoting verses A hasn't asked for, and without dismissing A's actual professional duty. A's task: defend the identity honestly, push back on B, and notice in real time when māyā's covering feature is speaking through you. After five minutes, swap and debrief: where did you feel the pull of mahā-māyā vs. yoga-māyā in the conversation itself?

    Objections & Responses
    • This is just a cosmic excuse for fatalism. If māyā is doing everything by Kṛṣṇa's arrangement, then I'm not responsible for my choices — I'm a puppet. Why bother with sādhana?
      Read the verse carefully — Prabhupāda quotes BG 3.27 precisely to name this trap: ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate. The bewildered soul thinks itself the doer; that is the disease, not the diagnosis. The verse does NOT say you have no agency. It says your agency is being mis-assigned. Mahā-māyā operates on the conditioned soul; yoga-māyā operates on the surrendered soul. The single act of choice you actually have is which side of that potency you put yourself under — and you make that choice every morning when you either chant or don't, every evening when you either offer the day's work to Kṛṣṇa or pocket it for the false ego. Fatalism is the false conclusion of the half-read verse. The full verse demands more responsibility, not less.
    • Calling other religious paths 'mahā-māyā' and only the bhakti path 'yoga-māyā' sounds sectarian and arrogant. Aren't all paths valid expressions of the same Absolute?
      Notice what the verse actually says: parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate — the Lord's potency is variously described. Prabhupāda's analogy is precise: one electricity, two functions. Heating and cooling are not equally valid for someone who needs to cool down. The distinction between yoga-māyā and mahā-māyā is not between religions or sects — it is the description of what happens to a soul under two different orientations: turning toward Kṛṣṇa (unmukha) or covered from Him (āvaraṇikā). A Christian who genuinely surrenders in love to God is being moved by yoga-māyā. A so-called Vaiṣṇava who chants mechanically while clinging to false ego is under mahā-māyā. The Gauḍīya line is personalist and specific — surrender is to the supreme Person, Kṛṣṇa, not to an impersonal Absolute that flattens distinctions. That is not arrogance; it is the honesty of saying that 'all rivers reach the same ocean' is itself an impersonalist slogan that the verse does not support. Mahātmānas tu māṁ pārtha daivīṁ prakṛtim āśritāḥ — those who take shelter of His divine nature are directed by yoga-māyā. The shelter is specific. The Person is specific.
    Analogy

    Viṣṇu-māyā — Bhagavān's own potency — will also appear with Kṛṣṇa, not as a separate goddess but as the very śakti by whom He works. She is to Him what the heat is to the fire — non-different in tattva, distinct in function. The verse stages the principle: where the Person appears, the Person's energy appears as His attendant, never as a rival.

    Important Words
    • prajāpati-patiḥ — Lord Brahmā, the master of the Prajāpatis
      Prajāpati (lord of progeny) + pati (master). Brahmā is the master of those who are themselves masters. The compound underscores his rank — yet he is still subordinate to Bhagavān, as established in verse 21.
    • vibhuḥ — all-powerful
      From vi-bhū, 'becoming all-pervasive, mighty.' Brahmā is vibhu within the universe; Kṛṣṇa is vibhu without limitation. The same word carries different scope depending on the subject.
    • āśvāsya — after pacifying
      Gerund of ā-śvas, 'to give breath, to console.' Brahmā specifically comforts Earth before leaving. A devotee in a position of authority does not depart without pastoral closure — the line between governance and care is not drawn.
    • sva-dhāma — his own planet, known as Brahmaloka
      Sva (own) + dhāma (abode). The same word used for Kṛṣṇa's own dhāma (Goloka, Vraja). The word's recurrence is doctrinally telling: every level of being has a sva-dhāma; the question is whose dhāma is final. Gauḍīya answer: Goloka.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After thus advising the demigods and pacifying mother earth, the very powerful Lord Brahmā, who is the master of all other Prajāpatis and is therefore known as Prajāpati-pati, returned to his own abode, Brahmaloka.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After thus advising the demigods and pacifying mother earth, the very powerful Lord Brahmā, who is the master of all other Prajāpatis and is therefore known as Prajāpati-pati, returned to his own abode, Brahmaloka.
    Commentary

    Iti indicates that here the message of Visnu as related by Brahma ends.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He gave orders according to what Viṣṇu repeated of Kṛṣṇa’s words. His qualification to give orders is stated. He was lord of the Prajāpatis like Marīci because he was powerful (vibhuḥ). The other meaning is that by helping bring about the appearance of Kṛṣṇa, his position as protector of the Prajāpatis and as a powerful figure became successful. He pacified the earth. “You are most fortunate. Your surface will be decorated very soon by Kṛṣṇa’s foot prints.” He went to Satyaloka to satisfy the personified Vedas and his associates who were situated far away from him at present by giving the news that Kṛṣṇa would appear on earth.
